column1: # Module 09 — eval harness mini. Format: Text<TAB>tags. Card law: anki/CARD-RULES.md
What are an eval's three irreducible parts? {{c1::Fixed tasks}} + {{c2::a scoring method}} + {{c3::blindness (the discipline not to peek)}}.
What are the two eval scoring families? {{c1::Programmatic — a checker decides}} · {{c2::rubric — a human grades blind against written criteria}}.
Why must rubric grading be blind? {{c1::You WILL favour the model you expect to win}} — shuffling + anonymising is the only honest fix.
What are the four properties of a good eval task? {{c1::Representative}} · {{c2::one skill per task}} · {{c3::verifiable}} · {{c4::crisply stated}}.
What is contamination in an eval? {{c1::The answer exists as memorised text}} — it measures recall of the internet, not capability.
Why is n=1 an anecdote when evaluating models? {{c1::Models are stochastic — single runs are noise}}; patterns across {{c2::task FAMILIES}} are the signal.
What does a per-family subtotal reveal that the total hides? {{c1::The capability profile}} — a model can win code and lose writing.
Model X felt smarter — what is the engineering translation? {{c1::No measurement occurred. Run the harness}}.
In module 09's 9–9 dead-heat fixture, what was the lesson? Equal totals with {{c1::OPPOSITE profiles}} — which model you want depends on {{c2::the JOB}}.
Why did fixture-B fail four programmatic tasks despite correct answers? {{c1::Extra prose around a correct answer still fails an exact-match contract}}.
Why write "reply with ONLY the number" in eval prompts? {{c1::The output contract makes programmatic checking possible}} — eval design IS prompt design.
What four things would make an eval harness lie to you? {{c1::Contaminated tasks}} · {{c2::leading/ambiguous prompts}} · {{c3::unblinded grading}} · {{c4::reading n=1 noise as signal}}.
What is the criteria-vs-vibes test? {{c1::A stranger applying your criteria reaches your score}} — "is it good?" fails instantly.
Module 09's eval method reapplies unchanged to which two bigger surfaces? {{c1::Agents}} · {{c2::RAG}} — same method, bigger surface.
